figures: Figure 1. Company observations over time in the retained partitions. Vertical markers denote the 2022 and 2024 observation-date boundaries. Unequal early coverage is part of the actual sample.

Figure 2. Held-out accuracy, balanced accuracy and AUC for all eight models. Dashed lines show the training-majority baseline. SVM is highlighted because it was selected on validation data. LR=Logistic Regression; RF=Random Forest; NB=Naive Bayes; GB=Gradient Boosting; DT=Decision Tree.
Figure 3. Precision, sensitivity and specificity at each model’s saved decision rule. The imbalance between class-specific detection rates is visible even when overall accuracy differs little.
Figure 4. Test ROC curves and AUCs from positive-class probabilities, except SVM, which uses its positive-oriented decision function. The diagonal is the no-ranking-skill reference.

Figure 5. Logistic Regression: test confusion matrix and score-based ROC curve. Counts sum to 261; actual non-positive and positive row totals are 110 and 151. The orange point is the saved native decision rule.

Figure 14. SVM permutation importance on validation rows, measured as the decrease in balanced accuracy over ten shuffles per feature. Error bars are shuffle standard deviations, not confidence intervals.
Figure 15. Logistic Regression coefficients after common clipping, imputation and standardisation. Coefficients describe the fitted model, not causal effects or significance tests.
